verdict.rationale: Smithery's maintained CLI gives agents commands to find and call tools on demand (`smithery tool find`, `tool get`, `tool call`, `mcp search`), so discovery happens at runtime rather than through preloaded definitions. However, this is a CLI command surface, not documented in-context meta-tools. The October 2026 shutdown of the hosted Connect/Toolbox services also leaves it unclear whether connection-backed tool loading still works. Missing for 10: documented MCP meta-tools (search/load tools) exposed to the agent, explicit evidence of context-window savings, confirmed post-shutdown working of connection-based tool get/call, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can search and load tools at runtime through meta-tools instead of having thousands of tool definitions stuffed into my context

citations.quote: smithery tool find [query], smithery tool get <connection> <tool>, smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]
Smithery CLI connects your agents to thousands of skills and MCP servers directly from the command line.
